regulatory_findings.value: €45,934.20 for shortage occupations, recent graduates (degree ≤3 years), and qualifying IT specialists; Federal Employment Agency (BA) approval generally required

citation.claim: Shortage occupations, recent graduates and qualifying IT specialists can obtain an EU Blue Card at a lower 2026 gross annual salary of at least €45,934.20 if the BA has approved the employment.

The reduced threshold applies where the occupation belongs to ISCO-08 groups 132, 133, 134, 21, 221, 222, 225, 226, 23 or 25, or where the academic degree was obtained no more than three years before the Blue Card application.

regulatory_findings.threshold_or_rule: IT specialists without a formal degree (§18g (2))
regulatory_findings.value: ISCO-08 groups 133 or 25, with ≥3 years of comparable experience in the last 7 years, BA approval, reduced salary threshold

citation.claim: Non-degree IT specialists may qualify for a Blue Card in ISCO groups 133 or 25 if they have at least three years of relevant university-level experience in the last seven years.

regulatory_findings.value: Generic COO/Head of Operations is often ISCO 1120 or 121 (not on the shortage list). Shortage applies only if duties are 132 (manufacturing/mining/construction/distribution managers), 133 (ICT service managers) or 134 (professional services managers).

citation.claim: Whether Head of Operations uses the reduced 2026 threshold is a duty-level ISCO classification question, not a job-title question. Product/ICT tracks more often land in 133 or 25.

caveats: This seed brief reconstructs the Germany EU Blue Card research methodology from public government and named-research sources. It is not a copy of any private research memo and is not immigration, legal, or tax advice.

Germany does not use US-style H-1B 'sponsorship.' The employer issues a qualifying contract; the candidate applies for the EU Blue Card. 'Sponsorship signal' here means public evidence of international professional hiring, not a visa lottery.

Job-title ≠ ISCO code. A Head of Operations uses the reduced 2026 threshold (€45,934.20) only if duties fall in groups 132, 133 or 134 (or another listed group). A Product / ICT track is more often 133 or 25. Confirm classification with the employer and the Ausländerbehörde.
Salary rows are official sector or occupation aggregates except the one row tagged SYNTHETIC. They are not an offer, a COO pay survey, or Glassdoor/Payscale scrapes.
The 2026 Blue Card thresholds (€50,700 / €45,934.20) are reset annually in the Federal Gazette and on Make it in Germany. Re-check before any application.
EY (€8.4bn, 716 rounds) and KfW/Dealroom (€7.2bn, 1,444 deals) are different VC coverage methods. Do not average them.
Degree recognition (Anabin / ZAB) and regulated-profession licensing are out of scope of this run and can block an otherwise salary-qualified Blue Card.
Figures accessed September 2026. Re-run live with an API key and optional MCP search before relying on them in a live search process.

tam_or_demand.claim: Germany's EU Blue Card under §18g AufenthG is the primary skilled-worker residence title for third-country academics; a qualifying job must last at least six months and match the applicant's qualification.

Two-track implication: Product / ICT leadership is much more likely to fall in shortage ISCO groups 133 or 25 (reduced Blue Card threshold, BA approval) than a generic Head of Operations / COO title, which often maps to ISCO 1120 or 121 and therefore uses the standard threshold unless duties are manufacturing, supply, ICT-service or professional-services management.

Full-time ICT employees in Germany earned a median gross monthly salary of €6,114 in 2025 (West €6,190, East €5,691), above the all-occupation median of €4,448 — a public demand/pay signal for the Product/ICT track.

funding_landscape.claim: German startups raised just under €8.4 billion in venture capital in 2025 across 716 publicly reported rounds, +19% versus 2024 by value but −5% by round count (EY Startup-Barometer 2026).

KfW Research, using Dealroom coverage, puts 2025 German VC investment at €7.2 billion across 1,444 deals (vs €7.4 billion in 2024). Treat the EY and KfW totals as methodologically different series, not a disagreement about a single number.

EY attributes more than 70% of 2025 German VC value to Software & Analytics (~€2.7 billion), Energy, and Health (~€1.1 billion); Bavaria led Länder with €3.3 billion, ahead of Berlin at ~€2.7 billion.
KfW reports a 2025 record for AI-related VC in Germany of about €2.9 billion, roughly two-fifths of its German VC total — relevant for Product-track hiring at AI-adopting scale-ups.
